intro.title: Generic useFetch<T>
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a reusable custom React hook called `useFetch<T>` that fetches data from an API. You will learn how to use TypeScript generics to make the hook flexible and type-safe, allowing it to return data of any specified type. The main technologies involved are React hooks (like `useState` and `useEffect`), TypeScript generics, and asynchronous JavaScript with `fetch`. By the end, you'll have a hook that handles loading and error states while providing strongly-typed data for your components.
intro.usecase: Generic useFetch<T> is essential in data-driven React applications where you need to fetch different types of data with consistent loading, error, and success states. In e-commerce dashboards, you'd use it to fetch product listings, user orders, and inventory data—each with different TypeScript interfaces but the same fetching logic. Admin panels use this pattern to load user profiles, analytics metrics, and audit logs while maintaining type safety across all API responses. This approach eliminates code duplication when building complex interfaces like data tables with filters, real-time notification feeds, or multi-step forms that fetch configuration data.
